blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
KPIs and supply chain dashboards at board level serve a different purpose from operational ones. The board is not trying to run the warehouse or chase a specific shipment; it is trying to understand whether the supply chain is healthy enough to support the company's strategy over the next two or three years. That means the board dashboard shows different numbers: service level trend over quarters, not daily OTIF; inventory days against industry benchmarks, not weekly stock counts; concentration risk by supplier and geography, not individual open orders. The board cares about direction, risk and resilience — not operational detail.

Mistakes happen when supply chain leaders show the board their own operational dashboards, which are dense, weekly, and completely uninterpretable by outsiders. The right instinct is to translate: to build a small, stable set of board-level indicators that tell the real story of the chain in language the board can act on.

Done well, this translation changes how the board sees the supply chain — from a cost centre to a source of strategic resilience.

items.q: According to the text, what is the board primarily trying to understand?
options: Which individual orders are still open
How to chase a specific delayed shipment
Whether the supply chain can support the company's strategy over the next few years
How the warehouse is run day to day
items.why: "it is trying to understand whether the supply chain is healthy enough to support the company's strategy over the next two or three years."

items.q: Which set of metrics belongs on a board-level dashboard, according to the text?
options: Line-by-line shipment tracking and hourly throughput
Individual supplier invoices and daily picking rates
Daily OTIF, weekly stock counts and individual open orders
Service level trend, inventory days against benchmarks and concentration risk
items.why: O texto contrasta as métricas de board (tendência, dias de estoque vs. benchmark, risco de concentração) com as operacionais.

items.q: Why do problems arise, according to the text?
options: The supply chain has too few metrics to report
Leaders show the board dense operational dashboards outsiders cannot interpret
Boards refuse to look at any supply chain data at all
The board demands more operational detail than leaders can provide
items.why: "Mistakes happen when supply chain leaders show the board their own operational dashboards, which are dense, weekly, and completely uninterpretable by outsiders."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Translation adds value when it is done deliberately
Resilience matters more to the board than daily throughput
A board dashboard should read differently from an operational one
The more granular the data shown to the board, the better its decisions
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que granularidade operacional torna o painel ilegível para o board — o oposto de melhor decisão.

items.q: The phrase "from a cost centre to a source of strategic resilience" suggests that…
options: Good translation can reframe how the board values the supply chain
The supply chain should be cut to reduce costs
The board should stop reviewing the supply chain entirely
Resilience and cost are the same measure
items.why: Inferência: a boa tradução muda a percepção — de despesa a fonte de resiliência estratégica.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry na preparação do board pack trimestral. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let me walk you through the new supply chain slide before it goes into the board pack. I've pulled the old one — that weekly operational view with forty-odd lines. Honestly, no one outside the function could read it, and I'm not sure it earned its place.

What I've put in its stead is six indicators. Six, no more. Service level as a trend over the last eight quarters, inventory days set against the industry benchmark, and concentration risk — how exposed we are by supplier and by geography. Then working capital tied up in stock, year on year, and total cost of ownership rather than unit cost, because unit cost flatters us and hides the freight.

Each of the six has an owner, a target and a review cadence. If a number moves the wrong way, the board knows exactly who to ask and when it gets looked at again.

The point isn't to show off how much we measure. It's the opposite. Cutting it down to six was the hard part — deciding what the board actually needs to act on, and leaving everything else in the operational pack where it belongs.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did Harry pull the old supply chain slide?
options: It was a dense weekly operational view outsiders could not read
It was missing the service level figures
It contained confidential supplier data
The board had asked for more detail
items.why: "that weekly operational view with forty-odd lines… no one outside the function could read it."

items.q: How many indicators does the new slide contain?
options: Six
Four
Eight
Twelve
items.why: "What I've put in its stead is six indicators. Six, no more."

items.q: Why does Harry prefer total cost of ownership over unit cost?
options: Unit cost is harder to calculate
The board specifically requested unit cost be removed
Total cost of ownership is updated more frequently
Unit cost flatters the numbers and hides freight
items.why: "total cost of ownership rather than unit cost, because unit cost flatters us and hides the freight."

items.q: When Harry says "I'm not sure it earned its place," he implies that…
options: The old slide did not justify the space it took in the pack
The board had never seen the slide before
Someone else had designed the slide badly
The slide was too expensive to produce
items.why: Inferência: 'earn its place' = justificar sua presença; ele sugere que a informação não valia o espaço.

items.q: What does Harry regard as the hard part of the work?
options: Assigning an owner to each metric
Collecting the underlying operational data
Deciding what to leave out and cutting the set down to six
Persuading the board to read the slide
items.why: Inferência: "Cutting it down to six was the hard part — deciding what the board actually needs to act on."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We hold a great deal of stock with a single supplier, so our concentration risk is high." Concentration risk is…
options: the risk of losing focus during long meetings
the danger of overstating inventory value
the exposure created by depending heavily on one supplier or region
the cost of concentrating production in one factory
items.why: Concentration risk = risco de concentração: exposição por depender demais de um fornecedor ou geografia.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Measuring inventory days against an industry ___ tells us whether we are lean or bloated."
options: benchmark
geography
instinct
purpose
items.why: Benchmark = referência: parâmetro do setor contra o qual se compara o próprio número.

items.q: "The weekly operational pack was uninterpretable to anyone outside the function." Uninterpretable means…
options: confidential and restricted
impossible to make sense of
printed at the wrong scale
updated too infrequently
items.why: Uninterpretable = não interpretável: que não se consegue entender ou ler.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "The board follows the ___ over eight quarters rather than a single monthly figure."
options: concentration risk
service level trend
total cost of ownership
cost centre
items.why: Service level trend = tendência de nível de serviço, acompanhada ao longo de vários trimestres.

items.q: "Reframed well, the supply chain stops being a mere cost centre." A cost centre is…
options: the office where invoices are processed
a part of the business seen only as an expense to control
a supplier that charges above market rates
the department that sets prices for customers
items.why: Cost centre = centro de custo: unidade vista apenas como despesa a ser contida, não como fonte de valor.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de board e reporte executivo. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new KPI pack before it goes to the board." To sign off on means to…
options: translate into plain language
formally approve
quietly shelve
circulate for comments
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the board dashboard from next quarter onwards." To roll out means to…
options: implement or introduce in stages
test in secret
summarise on one page
withdraw gradually
items.why: Roll out = implementar/introduzir de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on cutting the metric set to six." They…
options: postponed reading the pack
resisted or challenged the idea
rewrote the whole slide themselves
approved it without discussion
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Reporting a nicer unit cost would only paper over the freight problem." To paper over means to…
options: resolve for good
conceal a problem without solving it
document thoroughly
escalate to the board
items.why: Paper over = mascarar/disfarçar um problema sem realmente resolvê-lo.

items.q: "Six sharp indicators will move the needle on how the board sees the chain." This means they will…
options: make a noticeable, meaningful difference
require external auditing
add unnecessary complexity
take too long to compile
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível e relevante.
